theory.intro: A simple interest investment earns the same interest each year. Its total investment value increases by the same amount each year, so its value-time graph is a straight line.
facts: Simple interest is calculated on the principal only.
The yearly interest is the principal multiplied by the annual interest rate written as a decimal.
The total investment value is the principal plus the interest earned.
A total-value graph starts at the principal when time is $0$ years.
Plot time on the horizontal axis and total investment value on the vertical axis.
steps: Calculate the interest earned each year using the original principal.
Make a table of the total investment value at time $0$ and at the end of each year.
Choose suitable scales and label the axes Time (years) and Investment value.
Plot the values from the table and join the points with a straight line.

workedExamples.question_text: An amount of $\$6000$ is invested at $5\%$ p.a. simple interest for $4$ years. Make a table of its total value from time $0$ to year $4$, then draw a graph showing how the investment value changes.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Yearly interest $=6000\times0.05=\$300$.
At time $0$, the value is $\$6000$.
Year $1$: $6000+300=\$6300$.
Year $2$: $6300+300=\$6600$.
Year $3$: $6600+300=\$6900$.
Year $4$: $6900+300=\$7200$.
Label the horizontal axis Time (years) and the vertical axis Investment value.
Plot $(0,6000)$, $(1,6300)$, $(2,6600)$, $(3,6900)$ and $(4,7200)$.
Join the points with a straight line.

foundation.question_text: An amount of $\$1000$ is invested at $5\%$ p.a. simple interest for $3$ years. Make a table of its total value from time $0$ to year $3$, then draw the investment-value graph.
foundation.solution_text:
Yearly interest $=1000\times0.05=\$50$.
Time $0$: $\$1000$.
Year $1$: $1000+50=\$1050$.
Year $2$: $1050+50=\$1100$.
Year $3$: $1100+50=\$1150$.
Plot $(0,1000)$, $(1,1050)$, $(2,1100)$ and $(3,1150)$.
Join the points with a straight line, with time in years horizontally and investment value vertically.
